properties.title: Action-Conditioned World Model for Goal Plane Guidance in Robotic Neck Ultrasound

membership.reason: Action-conditioned latent CDiT ultrasound world model used in actor-critic RL to fine-tune a goal-conditioned robotic probe-guidance policy, evaluated in real-world closed-loop scanning.

properties.backbone: Frozen VAE + Conditional Diffusion Transformer (CDiT) world model + goal-conditioned temporal transformer actor-critic policy

properties.flow: Live US frames -> Frozen VAE -> Goal-conditioned policy (trained via frozen CDiT WM rollouts) -> 6-axis RM65-B robot + low-level force safety controller

properties.purpose: Protocol-driven sequential goal-plane probe guidance in robotic carotid and thyroid ultrasound.
properties.environment: Subject-disjoint offline trajectories (20 subjects) + real-world closed-loop robotic trials

properties.human_participant_roles: Human experts performing counterfactual-action identification (Section III-B, Table II) and live human subject(s) undergoing ethics-approved closed-loop robotic neck ultrasound scanning (Section III-D, Fig. 7, Table IV; CASIA ethics ref IA21-2502-020302).
properties.reporting_limits: Exact number of human expert raters, blinding protocol, inter-rater reliability, and exact number/demographics/volunteer-vs-patient status of human subjects scanned across the 20 real-world trials per task are not reported.

evidence_fragments.content: In real-world closed loop experiments, the framework achieves success rates of 70.0% for carotid guidance and 65.0% for thyroid guidance. These results demonstrate the potential of learned ultrasound dynamics for training goal-directed robotic probe navigation within protocol-constrained organ specific tasks.

As shown in Fig. 2, the model predicts the future ultrasound observation by jointly considering recent visual context, the relative probe motion, and the temporal offset. As stated in the problem formulation, we encode ultrasound frames into a compact latent representation using a frozen V AE encoder enc. Operating in the V AE latent space reduces the spatial redundancy of ultrasound images while preserving the speckle texture, anatomical boundaries, and acoustic shadow patterns that are important for navigation. To implement the world modelW, we employ a Conditional Diffusion Transformer (CDiT) [14] with learnable parameters θ. The functionf θ models the ultrasound dynamics by predicting noise during the diffusion process. The latent dynamics are modeled as follows. locator.section_or_table: Section III-C Table III action predictor evaluation

evidence_fragments.content: World-model-guided fine-tuning addresses different weaknesses of supervised learning across the two tasks. For carotid guidance, the supervised policy already predicts the active axis accurately, but performs poorly on several motion bins. Finetuning substantially improves the x, y, rx, ry, and rz bin accuracies, while Stop F1 increases from 0.835 to 0.883. However, z-bin accuracy decreases from 0.970 to 0.851. For thyroid guidance, supervised learning already achieves high accuracy on several motion bins, leaving less room for improvement. Fine-tuning mainly improves the weaker x-bin accuracy from 0.482 to 0.667 and Stop F1 from 0.704 to 0.762. These results suggest that world-model-guided fine-tuning can complement supervised learning by refining task-dependent weaknesses, although the improvements are not uniform across motion dimensions.

capability_assessments.rationale: Action-conditioned latent CDiT ultrasound world model used to fine-tune a goal-conditioned robotic probe-guidance policy via actor-critic RL, validated in real-world closed-loop scanning.

legacy_cells.B: Action-Conditioned World Model for Goal Plane Guidance in Robotic Neck Ultrasound
legacy_cells.C: Fan, Siqi, Liu, Ran, Yang, Zixuan, Fu, Xiaoyu, Gao, Xiaoqing, Xing, Yingqi, et al.
legacy_cells.S: Can the model predict future neck ultrasound observations under probe motion, and can a policy guide the probe to ordered target planes?
legacy_cells.T: Self-collected neck ultrasound trajectories from 20 people.
legacy_cells.V: Select corrective probe motions and stop decisions for sequential target-plane acquisition.
legacy_cells.AI: Ultrasound image frames; synchronized relative 6-DoF probe motions/poses; temporal offsets; previous probe actions and goal-plane image latents for the policy.
legacy_cells.AJ: Frozen VAE image encoder/decoder; Conditional Diffusion Transformer (CDiT) for latent ultrasound dynamics; temporal transformer for the goal-conditioned policy.
legacy_cells.AM: World-model CDiT conditions future latent tokens on encoded context, embedded relative probe motion, temporal offset and diffusion step; policy combines context latent tokens, previous-action tokens and pooled goal-plane latents.
legacy_cells.BD: Relative 6-DoF probe translation and rotation; temporal offset; translation/rotation normalized by dataset-specific scales. Policy outputs a single-axis motion bin.
legacy_cells.BI: Action-conditioned latent diffusion ultrasound world model (descriptive label; no distinct acronym stated).
legacy_cells.BS: Decoded predicted future ultrasound frame from the future latent state.
legacy_cells.BT: Goal-conditioned policy axis, motion-bin and stop heads.
legacy_cells.BU: Reward for progress toward and proximity to the active goal plane, correct stopping, and penalties for large or abrupt probe motions; actor-critic value estimates expected future return.
legacy_cells.BV: World-model diffusion noise-prediction MSE; weighted axis/bin/stop cross-entropy imitation loss; actor-critic policy updates from world-model reward and value-regression loss.
legacy_cells.CK: Maximize goal-plane progress/proximity and successful stopping, with penalties on action magnitude and changes between consecutive actions.
legacy_cells.DN: Self-collected neck ultrasound trajectory dataset (no separate dataset name stated).
legacy_cells.DQ: 20 people; 184 carotid, 150 thyroid and 17 random-sweep trajectories.
legacy_cells.EC: Real-robot closed-loop success: 70.0% for carotid guidance and 65.0% for thyroid guidance (abstract/conclusion).
legacy_cells.EE: Human experts compared predictions generated with the recorded action against predictions using incorrect actions; identification accuracy was reported.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with supervised-only policy, world-model fine-tuning raised final real-world success from 0.30 to 0.70 for carotid and 0.00 to 0.65 for thyroid.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablated goal conditioning in each training stage and compared supervised-only policies with world-model-guided fine-tuning; reported task-specific axis/bin accuracy and Stop F1.
legacy_cells.EL: Single-axis actions can fail when a target view requires coordinated multi-axis corrections, leaving residual pose errors; generalization beyond neck ultrasound is unverified.
legacy_cells.EM: For subject safety, only x, y, rx and rz were sent as position commands; z and ry were controlled by a low-level force-control module.
legacy_cells.ER: Ethical approval from the Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences local ethics committee; study reference IA21-2502-020302.
legacy_cells.FL: Ultrasound frames → frozen VAE latent context → conditional diffusion transformer conditioned on relative probe motion and Δt → decoded future ultrasound frame; a temporal-transformer policy combines context, action history and goal-bank latents, then outputs axis/bin/stop actions and is fine-tuned with frozen-world-model rewards for closed-loop robot guidance.
legacy_cells.FM: Learn neck-ultrasound action dynamics with a latent conditional diffusion world model and use its predicted action consequences to fine-tune a goal-conditioned probe-motion policy for sequential target-plane guidance.
legacy_cells.FN: In real-world closed-loop experiments, reported success was 70.0% for carotid and 65.0% for thyroid guidance; authors also report action-dependent anatomy predictions and task-specific gains from world-model-guided fine-tuning.
legacy_cells.FO: The single-axis action formulation cannot make coordinated multi-axis corrections; probe-induced image changes are not separated from physiology/contact variation; generalization beyond neck scanning is unverified; force information is not an input to either learned model.
legacy_cells.FP: Expand the dataset to more diverse anatomies, incorporate respiratory/temporal motion cues, and add force-torque measurements for pressure-aware dynamics and contact-stable guidance.
legacy_cells.FQ: Expert trajectories and plane annotations are expensive, while explicit physics-based ultrasound simulators struggle to reproduce tissue deformation, probe pressure and acoustic artifacts.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence supports action-conditioned local neck-ultrasound dynamics and robot-guidance feasibility only; the action-discrimination experiment is not causal identification, and the paper does not establish broad anatomical generalization, clinical benefit or external validation.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M7 Outcome & causal layer; M8 Planner; M9 Safety & governance
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Keep the learned patient/scene simulator separate from the planner objective; constrain candidate actions and report closed-loop decision quality alongside model fidelity.
